title: In Situ Visualization of TACO1-Mediated Efficient Mitochondrial Translation Elongation
projectDescription: Isolation of CO1 mRNA ribonucleoprotein complexes from TACO1 KO and WT HEK293T cells
sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein solution samples (2 experimental conditions, 3 replicates/condition) were partially dried under vacuum and then supplemented with equal volume of 10% SDS resulting in a final concentration of ~5% SDS. The samples were then processed for trypsin digestion using Micro S-TrapsTM (Protifi) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, samples were reduced using tris-2(-carboxyethyl)-phosphine (TCEP) at 55 °C for 15 min, alkylated using methyl methanethiosulfonate (MMTS) at room temperature for 10 min, and then digested with 2 mg trypsin at 47 °C for 1 hour. Following this incubation, 40 uL of 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB) was added and peptides were eluted using centrifugation. Elution was repeated once. A third elution using 35mL of 50% acetonitrile (ACN) was performed. The eluted peptides were then dried under vacuum. Peptide digests were acidified with TFA to 0.1% (v:v) and desalted using 2 μg capacity ZipTips (Millipore) according to manufacturer instructions. Following drying under vacuum, peptides were re-solubilized in 0.1% formic acid (FA). LC-MS/MS analysis using 20% peptides by volume, was performed using a nanoElute ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) system (plug-in V2.1.60.0; Bruker, Bremen, Germany) coupled to a Bruker Tims TOF Pro2 mass spectrometer (Bruker, Bremen, Germany), equipped with a CaptiveSpray source and a 20μm zero dead volume (ZDV) Sprayer. Peptides were loaded onto a Thermo Fisher (Waltham) PepMap Neo C18 trap column (300mm X 5mm, 5mm particle size) and then separated on PepSep Series reverse-phase C18 column (15cm X 150μm, 1.5μm particle size) from Bruker (Bremen, Germany). The column temperature was maintained at 50°C using an integrated Bruker Column Toaster (Bremen, Germany). The column was equilibrated using 4 column volumes before loading samples in 100% buffer A (99.9% Fisher Optima® LC/MS water, 0.1% FA), with both steps performed at 800 bars. The trap column was equilibrated was equilibrated at 200 bars. Samples were separated at 500 nl/min using a linear gradient from 2% to 35% buffer B (99.9% Fisher Optima® LC/MS acetonitrile, 0.1% FA) over 40.0 minutes before ramping to 95% buffer B (in 0.5 minutes) and sustained at 95% buffer B for 4.5 minutes (total separation method time 45.0 min). The Bruker Tims TOF Pro 2 was operated in DIA-PASEF mode using Tims Control v. 5.0.2. Settings for the MS method were as follows: Mass Range 100 to 1700m/z, 1/K0 Start 0.6 V.·/cm2 End 1.4 V·s/cm2, TIMS Ramp and accumulation time 75ms, Capillary Voltage 1700V, Dry Gas 3 l/min, Dry Temp 200°C, DIA-PASEF settings: 18 MS/MS scans (50m/z windows, 0.21 1/K0 windows, total cycle time 0.74), mass range 300 to 1200, and CID collision energy 20eV (at 0.60, 1/K0) to 65eV (at 1.60, 1/K0). The analysis was performed at The Herbert Wertheim UF Scripps Institute for Biomedical Innovation & Technology, Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics Core Facility (RRID:SCR_023576).
dataProcessingProtocol: Quantitative analysis of the label free experiments was performed simultaneously with protein identification using DIA-NN 1.8 (85). Spectral libraries based on Uniprot Human proteome and common contaminant FASTA files were created in silico by Deep learning option in DIA-NN using the same enzyme and modification preferences as the search. Search criteria were as follows; N-terminus Methionine excision and static modification of Carbamidometylation / +45.988 Da (C); the precursor and fragment ion mass tolerances were set to 1e-05 (MS2) and 1e-05 (MS1) based on previous analysis. The enzyme was Trypsin (specific) with a maximum of 1 missed cleavage. The Precursor and Fragment Ion m/z range were set to 100-1700. Protein inference algorithm was set with the optional command --relaxed-prot-inf and -repot-lib-info options to make downstream analysis convenient. Match between runs (MBR), cross-run normalization was set to RT-based. The exported main report.tsv file was imported into R Studio (86, 87) through MSstatsConvert 1.12.1 to be analyzed using MSstats 4.10.1 (88). No normalization or imputation was applied due to the nature of the experiment. Each compound and its control were compared to each other using a one-sided test since only the proteins that were higher in KO samples. To be able to appropriately apply FDR of 5% to one sided test, FDRestimation 1.0.1 (89) package was used. FDR <0.05 were considered statistically significant (90). The analysis was performed at University of Florida UF Scripps Biomedical Research Bioinformatics and Statistics Core Facility (RRID:SCR_023048).
